newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to announce new telecoms rules Jan 1997.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to announce new telecoms rules Jan 1997.

text.p: Singapore said on Wednesday it would unveil new regulations for operators of telecommunications services and networks in January 1997.

Communications minister Mah Bow Tan told a news conference the rules, to be drawn up by the Telecommunications Authority of Singapore, would "ensure fair, effective and sustainable competition amongst operators".
He gave no details of the new rules but said they would cover the areas of interconnection, numbering, infrastructure sharing and anti-competitive behaviour.
He said the need for regulation "will not diminish with liberalisation of basic services in 2000".
Mah said the new regulations were needed to minimise unnecessary duplication of resources, inconvenience to consumers and to ensure efficient installation of new networks.
Mah said upgrading the infrastructure was vital to maintaining Singapore's position as a business hub.
Full details of the regulatory package would be released in advance of the pre-qualification tender for basic telecoms licenses in Singapore scheduled for March 1997.
